correctness.rationale: For q≥3 a repeated-colour pair forces its unique joining line monochromatic. Two intersecting monochromatic lines propagate their common colour to any outside point by a transversal through that point avoiding the two parallel directions and their intersection (at most three excluded of q+1≥4). Since ≥2 colours required, all monochromatic lines parallel. Distinct parallel mono-lines cannot share a colour (a transversal would force a crossing mono-line), and all other points have fresh singleton colours. Converse by checking a transversal meets a selected line at most once. Therefore the partition count is 1+(q+1)(2^q−1), coefficient (q+1)C(q,k), colour spectrum q²−k(q−1), missing q(q−2), and labeled falling-factorial polynomial; q=2 every nonconstant colouring is lean. Independent exhaustive 21147 partitions at q=3 give 4+12+12+1=29 and q=2 yields 14.
